tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session opened a WordPress post at 'http://localhost:8000/?p=8', clicked the Reply link for comment id=15 (replytocom=15), filled the comment textarea and the author/email inputs, and clicked the submit control. The new comment appeared and the page anchored at a comment id (e.g. #comment-20).

Task Definition:
- Create a reusable, deterministic tool that replies to an existing comment on a WordPress post by: 1) activating the reply context for a given comment id, 2) filling required comment form fields (comment, author, email), 3) optionally filling website, 4) submitting the form, and 5) verifying that the comment appears.

Action Plan:
1. Navigate to the post URL with the replytocom parameter (direct URL navigation replaces several UI clicks and is deterministic).
2. Wait briefly for the DOM and reply script to move the respond form into position.
3. Fill textarea[name='comment'] using form-scoped selectors with fallbacks and recorded elementHash backup.
4. Fill input[name='author'] with the provided author value.
5. Fill input[name='email'] with the provided email value.
6. Optionally fill input[name='url'] with website value (no conditional branching; an empty string leaves it blank).
7. Click the form submit control using form-scoped submit selector (recorded elementHash backup included).
8. Wait for submission and page reload/anchor, then extract page content to verify the presence of the new comment.

Variable Identification:
- post_url (string): exact post page URL to operate against (required).
- replytocom (string): numeric comment id to reply to (required) — used to build the navigation URL.
- comment (string): reply body text (required) — maps to name='comment'.
- author (string): commenter name (required) — maps to name='author'.
- email (string): commenter email (required) — maps to name='email'.
- website (string): optional website (maps to name='url').
- wait_seconds_after_navigation (number): optional small wait to handle dynamic JS movement of the form.

Step Optimization:
- Replaced the UI sequence 'find Reply link -> click' with direct navigation to '{post_url}?replytocom={replytocom}#respond', which reliably sets the reply parent and anchors to the respond form. This removes a flaky click-on-link step.
- Use form-scoped CSS selectors (form#commentform ...) first to avoid ambiguous matches and ensure exactly one element is targeted within the form scope.
- Include recorded elementHash values from the original run as deterministic backups if selectors fail or to aid debugging.
- Added short waits after navigation and after submit to mitigate timing issues observed in previous runs and the failure logs.

Constraints and Decisions:
- The tool assumes WordPress-standard form fields (name attributes: comment, author, email, url) because the recorded session used those. If a site has custom markup, callers can still use the post_url and provide values; robust selector overrides are not included to keep the tool single-purpose and deterministic.
- Cookie-consent toggle and other non-essential optional interactions are omitted to keep the tool focused on the essential flow of posting a reply.

Required selectors backed by recorded element hashes:
- Textarea: form#commentform textarea#comment (elementHash: 67f1dce8d0)
- Author: form#commentform input#author (elementHash: 085915c9f4)
- Email: form#commentform input#email (elementHash: cedb6c9f0b)
- Submit: form#commentform input[type='submit'] or form#commentform button[type='submit'] (elementHash: 777443c52e)

This tool strictly implements the one task 'reply to existing comment' with deterministic navigation and form interactions and includes a verification extraction at the end.
name: reply_to_comment_wordpress
description: Reply to an existing WordPress comment on a post by activating the Reply context (replytocom), filling the comment form fields, and submitting the comment. Uses standard WordPress form selectors with robust, form-scoped fallbacks and element-hash backups recorded during the original run.

steps.description: Navigate to the post URL with the replytocom parameter to activate the reply context and anchor the page at the respond form.
Allow the page to render and for JavaScript reply handlers to move the form into reply position. The value is conservative; callers may set wait_seconds_after_navigation if needed.
Fill the main comment textarea (form-scoped selectors first, then common fallbacks). Uses recorded elementHash as a stable backup.
Fill the author/name input. Uses form-scoped selector first and recorded elementHash as a backup.
Fill the email input. Uses form-scoped selectors with fallback and recorded elementHash.
Fill the website/url input if provided. This field is optional; sending an empty string leaves it blank.
steps.cssSelector: form#commentform input#url, form#commentform input[name='url'], input#url, input[name='url']

steps.description: Click the comment form submit control (Post Comment). Uses form-scoped submit selector and recorded elementHash as a backup.
Wait briefly for the form submission to process and the page to reload or anchor to the new comment.
Attempt to locate the newly posted comment by searching the page for the provided author name and comment text. Returns extracted page content for verification.
steps.goal: Confirm that a comment with author '{author}' and text '{comment}' appears on the page (used to verify successful posting).

input_schema.name: post_url
input_schema.description: Full URL of the post page (example: 'http://localhost:8000/?p=8'). The tool will navigate to this URL and add the replytocom fragment.

input_schema.name: replytocom
input_schema.description: Numeric comment id to reply to (the 'replytocom' query parameter). Example: '15' to reply to comment id=15.

input_schema.name: comment
input_schema.description: The reply text to post. Maps to the comment form field name='comment'. Required by the site.

input_schema.name: author
input_schema.description: Author/name to post with the comment. Maps to the input name='author'. Required by the site.

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Email address for the comment. Maps to input name='email'. Required by the site.

input_schema.name: website
input_schema.description: Optional website/URL to include with the comment. Maps to input name='url'. Leave empty if not needed.

input_schema.name: wait_seconds_after_navigation
input_schema.description: Seconds to wait after navigating to the reply URL before interacting with the form (default behavior: short wait to allow DOM updates). Use small positive numbers like 1 or 2. Optional.
